segments.contextBefore: `apns-expiration`
segments.contextAfter: The date when the notification expires. This value represents a UNIX epoch expressed in seconds (UTC). If the value is nonzero, APNs stores the notification and attempts delivery at least once, repeating as necessary until the specified date. If the value is `0`, APNs attempts to deliver the notification only once and doesn’t store it. Providing a nonzero expiration for a channel created with the No Message Stored storage policy results in message rejection. ![None](https://docs-assets.developer.apple.com/published/67dc4b07a8d84366d4cc0e812eb40b4a/spacer.png) A single APNs attempt may involve retries over multiple network interfaces and connections of the destination device. These retries often span some time period, depending on network characteristics. Additionally, a push notification may take some time on the network after APNs sends it to the device. APNs makes best efforts to honor the expiry date without any guarantee. If the value is nonzero, the notification may deliver after the specified timestamp. If the value is `0`, the notification may deliver with some delay.
